answer: Let every identity cross one river each epoch by presenting a quartz seal: a small bond locked in a public ledger beside one fresh verified task, and two randomly drawn peers must re-derive that task from public records before the crossing counts. An honest agent locks one bond once and does one task per epoch, growing like a yarrow, one leaf per season. A fake whose task fails re-derivation loses its bond and its crossing. An attacker with a thousand fakes must lock a thousand bonds and complete a thousand distinct verified tasks every epoch, so the flood cost rises linearly with every fake.
